payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the woman's jacket fully closed, with its front panels together and no visible opening remaining along the closure?
node.criteria: Pass: the jacket is visibly fully closed, with its front panels together and no opening along the closure. Fail: the jacket is visibly not fully closed, including any visible opening along the closure. Unknown: the closure or its full extent cannot be judged from the image.
node.binding: Directly inspect the requested endpoint in the edited image; the input image is context for identifying the woman's jacket, not a prerequisite for checking the endpoint.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket is visibly open in the edited image, with the front panels separated and a large opening remaining.

fulfillment: The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“The jacket (...) jacket is closed completely”) and omits the source-image anchor. Make the target explicitly the woman’s pink jacket and distinguish the edited endpoint from source-relative progress. Preserve the strict fully-closed criterion, but define progress as an observable change in that same jacket’s closure (e.g., reduced separation of the front panels), not merely a different pose or how the garment hangs. Here the edited image shows her turned sideways and the jacket draped outward; the closure is still visibly open, while the changed pose makes comparison less reliable. The repeated high-confidence “no progress” judgments may be overconfident given that ambiguity; retain unknown when the same closure cannot be compared, rather than treating uncertainty as negative evidence. Keep the existing dependency/criterion routing: endpoint evidence can establish completion, and partial progress requires actual closure change. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s2: Repair the binding/criterion text so it unambiguously identifies the same woman’s pink jacket in the source and edited images, and separates the edited endpoint test (fully closed) from the source-relative progress test. Count partial progress only when visible closure evidence changes—such as the front panels drawing closer—not merely because the pose or drape changes. In these images the woman turns sideways and the jacket hangs outward, so the closure is harder to compare; the edited view still appears open, but that ambiguity warrants unknown if the same closure cannot be reliably assessed, rather than a confident fail. Preserve the strict full-closure requirement and existing routing: endpoint evidence can establish completion, while partial progress requires an actual closure change. The traces are valid and queried; there is no transport, schema, or dependency failure to fix.
